title: DRE schedule occurrences, format 1
description: What `dre schedule ls --output json` prints: when the project's schedules fire within a window, with the command to run each firing. New fields may appear within format 1; consumers should ignore fields they don't know. See docs/schedule-ls.md.

dre_schedule_version.description: The format's version. Removing or renaming a field, or changing what a hash covers, needs a new one.

dre_version.description: The DRE version that wrote it.

split.description: True with `--split`: one occurrence per report and Set instead of one per firing.

project_hash.description: Over every schedule's definition hash, whatever was asked for: unchanged means no schedule changed.

schedules.description: The schedules asked for, by name, including paused ones and ones under `problems`.

occurrences.description: In firing order, then by key.

problems.description: Schedules that can't be expanded; they have no occurrences.

set.description: The Set, or null for a report without Sets.

definition_hash.description: Over the resolved timing (named or inline), the firing timezone, vars, `enabled` and the Bindings. Opaque: the same definition gives the same hash within a format version.

enabled.description: False for a paused schedule (`enabled: false`), which has no occurrences.

timing.description: The timings.yml entry it uses, or null for an inline timing.

timezone.description: The timezone it fires in: its own (or its timing's), then the project's, then UTC.

fires_at_local.description: The same instant in the firing timezone, with its offset, e.g. `2026-09-01T16:00:00+10:00`.

run_date.description: The firing's date in its timezone: the run's `run.date`.

invocation.description: The command that runs it, from the project directory. It never holds a target, profile or credentials.
